house_of_wisdom.name: House of Wisdom
house_of_wisdom.summary: Major intellectual center in Abbasid Baghdad that housed a vast library and translation institute.

al_khwarizmi.name: Al-Khwarizmi
al_khwarizmi.summary: Persian mathematician, astronomer, and geographer whose works founded algebra and introduced algorithms.

algebra.name: Algebra
algebra.summary: Mathematical discipline founded by Al-Khwarizmi for solving equations through systematic transformation.

al_kindi.name: Al-Kindi
al_kindi.summary: First major Islamic philosopher who synthesized Greek philosophy with Islamic thought.

ibn_sina.name: Ibn Sina (Avicenna)
ibn_sina.summary: Persian polymath whose "Canon of Medicine" was the standard medical text in Europe and the Islamic world for 600 years.

canon_of_medicine.name: Canon of Medicine
canon_of_medicine.summary: Ibn Sina\'s medical encyclopedia that systematized all known medical knowledge and remained authoritative for six centuries.

ibn_al_haytham.name: Ibn al-Haytham (Alhazen)
ibn_al_haytham.summary: Arab scientist who founded optics as an experimental science and pioneered the scientific method.

optics.name: Optics in the Golden Age
optics.summary: The science of light and vision as developed by Golden Age scholars, founded by Ibn al-Haytham.

translation_movement.name: Translation Movement
translation_movement.summary: Massive project to translate Greek, Persian, Indian, and Syriac scientific works into Arabic.

al_razI.name: Al-Razi (Rhazes)
al_razI.summary: Persian physician and alchemist who distinguished smallpox from measles and pioneered clinical observation.

astrolabe.name: Astrolabe
astrolabe.summary: Sophisticated astronomical instrument for solving problems relating to time, position, and celestial motion.

astronomy.name: Astronomy in the Golden Age
astronomy.summary: Highly advanced astronomical science developed in the Islamic world, combining Greek, Persian, and Indian traditions.

algebra_development.name: Development of Algebra
algebra_development.summary: The evolution of algebra from Al-Khwarizmi\'s rhetorical algebra to symbolic notation.

maragha_school.name: Maragha School
maragha_school.summary: School of astronomers at the Maragha Observatory who developed alternatives to Ptolemaic astronomy.

paper_making.name: Paper Making
paper_making.summary: Introduction and spread of papermaking technology from China through the Islamic world to Europe.

ibn_rushd.name: Ibn Rushd (Averroes)
ibn_rushd.summary: Andalusian philosopher and jurist whose commentaries on Aristotle shaped medieval European thought.

al_ghazali.name: Al-Ghazali
al_ghazali.summary: Influential Islamic theologian, jurist, and mystic who critiqued excessive rationalism in philosophy.

medicine_golden_age.name: Medicine in the Golden Age
medicine_golden_age.summary: Medical science as practiced and advanced in the Islamic world, combining Greek theory with clinical observation.

al_biruni.name: Al-Biruni
al_biruni.summary: Persian scholar who made groundbreaking contributions to astronomy, geography, and comparative religion.

al_zahrawi.name: Al-Zahrawi (Abulcasis)
al_zahrawi.summary: Andalusian surgeon whose medical encyclopedia was the standard surgical text in Europe for 500 years.

ibn_al_nafis.name: Ibn al-Nafis
ibn_al_nafis.summary: Arab physician who discovered pulmonary circulation 300 years before William Harvey.

philosophy_golden_age.name: Philosophy in the Golden Age
philosophy_golden_age.summary: The philosophical tradition that synthesized Greek philosophy with Islamic theology.

al_farabi.name: Al-Farabi
al_farabi.summary: Central Asian philosopher and political theorist who systematized Islamic philosophy and wrote on the ideal state.

omar_khayyam.name: Omar Khayyam
omar_khayyam.summary: Persian polymath who solved cubic equations geometrically and is also renowned for his poetry.

al_zarqali.name: Al-Zarqali
al_zarqali.summary: Andalusian astronomer and instrument maker who invented the universal astrolabe and improved astronomical tables.

nasir_al_din_tusi.name: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi
nasir_al_din_tusi.summary: Persian polymath who founded the Maragha Observatory and developed the Tusi couple, influencing Copernican astronomy.

ibn_al_shatir.name: Ibn al-Shatir
ibn_al_shatir.summary: Damascene astronomer whose lunar and planetary models were mathematically identical to Copernicus\' later formulations.

ulugh_beg.name: Ulugh Beg
ulugh_beg.summary: Timurid sultan, mathematician, and astronomer who built the world\'s largest observatory and compiled a stellar catalog of unprecedented accuracy.

al_battani.name: Al-Battani
al_battani.summary: Arab astronomer and mathematician who made remarkably accurate astronomical observations and improved Ptolemy\'s star catalog.

hunayn_ibn_ishaq.name: Hunayn ibn Ishaq
hunayn_ibn_ishaq.summary: Nestorian Christian translator, physician, and scholar who led the translation of Greek medical texts into Arabic.

al_idrisi.name: Al-Idrisi
al_idrisi.summary: Arab geographer and cartographer who created the most accurate world map and geographical encyclopedia of the pre-modern era.

ibn_khaldun.name: Ibn Khaldun
ibn_khaldun.summary: Arab historian, philosopher, and social scientist whose Muqaddimah laid foundations for modern historiography and sociology.

al_jazari.name: Al-Jazari
al_jazari.summary: Greatest mechanical engineer of the medieval Islamic world, known for his automata and programmable machines.

banu_musa.name: Banu Musa Brothers
banu_musa.summary: Three Persian brothers who produced the "Book of Ingenious Devices," a major work on mechanical engineering and automata.

thabit_ibn_qurra.name: Thabit ibn Qurra
thabit_ibn_qurra.summary: Sabian mathematician, physician, and translator who made fundamental contributions to number theory and geometry.

al_karaji.name: Al-Karaji
al_karaji.summary: Persian mathematician who freed algebra from geometry by arithmetizing algebraic operations.

al_samawal.name: Al-Samawal
al_samawal.summary: Arab mathematician who developed techniques for polynomial arithmetic and division.

ibn_sahl.name: Ibn Sahl
ibn_sahl.summary: Persian mathematician and optician who discovered the law of refraction (Snell\'s law) 600 years before Snell.

al_farghani.name: Al-Farghani
al_farghani.summary: Central Asian astronomer whose summary of Ptolemaic astronomy became a standard textbook in Europe and the Islamic world.

qusta_ibn_luqa.name: Qusta ibn Luqa
qusta_ibn_luqa.summary: Melkite Christian translator, physician, and philosopher who bridged Greek and Arabic medicine and science.

al_majriti.name: Al-Majriti
al_majriti.summary: Andalusian mathematician, astronomer, and alchemist who established science in Islamic Spain.

fatima_al_fihri.name: Fatima al-Fihri
fatima_al_fihri.summary: Arab woman who founded the University of al-Qarawiyyin, the oldest existing degree-granting university in the world.

mariam_al_astrulabi.name: Mariam al-Astrulabi
mariam_al_astrulabi.summary: 10th-century Syrian female astronomer and astrolabe maker, one of the few known women scientists of the Golden Age.

lubana.name: Lubana of Cordoba
lubana.summary: Andalusian female mathematician and librarian who served at the Library of Cordoba.

abbas_ibn_firnas.name: Abbas ibn Firnas
abbas_ibn_firnas.summary: Andalusian polymath who made the first recorded attempt at controlled human flight and invented various devices.

ibn_bajjah.name: Ibn Bajjah (Avempace)
ibn_bajjah.summary: Andalusian philosopher, astronomer, and physician who developed a naturalistic philosophy and anticipated Galilean motion.

ibn_tufayl.name: Ibn Tufayl
ibn_tufayl.summary: Andalusian philosopher and physician whose novel "Hayy ibn Yaqzan" explored the nature of reason and revelation.
